$comment: THE DECLARED SERVICE LEVELS FOR SELF-HEALING. This file is the single source; the L10
playbook describes it in prose and layer-10-audit.ps1 reads it, but neither is
authoritative.
It exists because the design that retired the seeded-CVE model says the window must be
DECLARED in configuration, not inherited from a default: 'this repository has twice been
bitten by criteria silently adopting a timeout nobody chose'. layer-10-audit.ps1
therefore SKIPs rather than assuming a number when this file is missing or malformed - a
criterion that invents its own pass line is not measuring anything.
Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-05-operationalize-self-healing-design.md sections 4-6.
Per source and per severity, NEVER averaged into one number - a blended figure hides
the slice that is not moving, which is the failure the compliance platform was built
to avoid. Values are the spec's section 5 table.
The clock starts when the finding is CREATED and stops when it is closed. A finding
with no upstream fix does not consume its SLO: it is pending-solution, which holds and
ages without failing, and V10.4 is what stops that state becoming a dumping ground.
TWO SCALES, BOTH DECLARED. critical/high/medium/low are the CVSS-aligned bands that
Dependabot and code scanning's security_severity_level use. error/warning/note are the
OTHER scale: a code-scanning alert on a non-security rule carries no
security_severity_level, so the audit falls back to rule.severity, which speaks in
those words instead.
The first run after this model shipped reported 13 findings as 'the policy declares no
SLO for severity note' - refusing to measure what nobody had declared rather than
inventing a number, which is the behaviour we want and also a gap in this file. They
are declared here rather than mapped silently in code, because a band the policy does
not name is precisely the thing a reader needs to be able to see is missing.
error tracks high; warning and note track the 30-day tier.
V10.2 asks that every closure be traceable. 'Since the last audit' is not a boundary
this script can read - reports are committed but an audit may be re-run, skipped, or
run twice in an hour - so the window is declared instead. 30 days covers a monthly
compliance cycle with room for a gap, and every closure inside it must carry either a
complete heal trail or an explicit dismissal record.
A lane whose MECHANISM does not exist yet, deferred with a DEADLINE rather than
excused indefinitely. Its findings do not count against V10.1 until the date below;
on that date the deferral stops applying by itself, and the criterion goes red again
if the lane still has no mechanism.
THE EXPIRY IS THE POINT. An exclusion that cannot expire is exactly the dumping
ground V10.4 exists to prevent, one level up. The audit prints the deferred count,
the expiry and the days remaining on EVERY run, and prints DEFERRAL EXPIRED after the
date - so this cannot be quietly forgotten.
A deadline, not an amnesty. The findings are real, and they stay visible.

container-image.reason: Lane 3 has no automated path on this subscription: ACR Tasks returns TasksOperationsNotAllowed (spec section 8, P1 - reproduced twice, on two registries in two resource groups), and the documented scheduled-rebuild fallback is not built yet. Counting base-image findings against a heal SLO states something true and unactionable.
container-image.unblockedBy: the scheduled rebuild in spec sections 8 and 11, or an Azure support request granting ACR Tasks

$comment: Findings for which NO automated path exists, so V10.1 must not count them as a
draining backlog and V10.4 must not demand an upstream fix for them. Each entry needs
a reason: an unexplained entry is how an exclusion list becomes a place to hide a
finding nobody wants to fix.
Empty by design. Add an entry only when the class genuinely has no automated fix path,
and say why here rather than in a commit message nobody will find.
Manifests whose findings are deliberate and are NOT part of the operational backlog.
apps/vuln-lab holds knowingly-vulnerable pins. Since the 2026-09-05 design it is no
longer load-bearing for any criterion - it is a manual demonstration generator, armed
deliberately by a human when the queue is empty or the chain needs exercising in front
of an audience. Its findings must therefore not age against an SLO the estate never
intended to meet: the package is excluded from the root npm workspaces, is never
imported by any deployed application, and is not built into any container image.
This is an exclusion from the BACKLOG, not from visibility. The alerts still exist,
V10.3 still proves the surface was readable, and the audit reports how many findings
were excluded and why, so an empty backlog can never be manufactured by adding a path
here unnoticed.
